title: SC to hear 22nd Amendment challenges today | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 1 September 2026 09:10
-     - 15

The Supreme Court will today commence hearings on a series of petitions challenging the constitutionality of the Government’s controversial proposed 22nd Amendment to the Constitution, taking the contested Bill into the next stage of judicial scrutiny following its presentation to Parliament.

The petitions, filed by several parties challenging the proposed constitutional amendment, are expected to be considered by a five-member Supreme Court bench.

The bench will be headed by Chief Justice Preethi Padman Surasena. The other members are Supreme Court Justices Achala Wengappuli, Arjuna Obeysekera, Sampath Abeykoon and Gihan Kulatunga.

Some of the petitioners challenging the proposed 22A to extend the retirement age of higher-court judges had called for the Chief Justice to recuse himself from the case while other asked for a full-bench.

title: ICRC says sustained, collective efforts critical to address issue of missing persons | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 1 September 2026 09:07
-     - 16

The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) on 30 August honoured the thousands of people around the world who are either missing or separated from their families due to armed conflict, violence, disasters and migration, standing in solidarity with families who endure the pain of not knowing the fate of their loved ones.

In Sri Lanka, the ICRC said thousands of families of missing persons from all communities across the country are still waiting for answers. Families of missing persons have the right to know what has happened to their loved ones. Unable to grieve, find closure or rebuild their lives, these families often struggle to meet the emotional, economic, legal, administrative, and social challenges posed by the absence of their missing loved one and the uncertainty that comes with it.

Addressing the needs of families of missing persons is a complex, multi-faceted process. Families are key partners and rights-holders and they are at the heart of this process. While national authorities have the primary responsibility to address their needs, local stakeholders can contribute to a broader, sustained response by building a comprehensive framework of support to address the diverse needs of families. Central to this is the search itself, a vital step toward the clarification of the fate and whereabouts of missing persons, involving collaborative action by multiple stakeholders.

Presently in Sri Lanka, the ICRC implements the Missing Persons Project which aims to foster a sustainable response to the issue of missing persons by supporting families, strengthening national and local capacities and enabling coordinated, state-led and community-based efforts to clarify the fate and whereabouts of the missing. 

Addressing the issue of missing persons is also crucial for peace and reconciliation. Unresolved cases can perpetuate trauma, deepen grievances and hinder community healing long after violence has ended. Sustained political commitment is necessary to resolve the issue in the long-term, even decades after an armed conflict.

title: Ravi Karunanayake released on bail in NLB corruption case | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 1 September 2026 09:07
-     - 20

Former Finance Minister and New Democratic Front (NDF) MP Ravi Karunanayake, who was arrested by the Commission to Investigate Allegations of Bribery or Corruption (CIABOC) over allegations that three employees recruited for a special project of the National Lotteries Board (NLB) were deployed for his political activities, causing a loss to the Government, was yesterday ordered to be released on bail by Colombo Additional Magistrate Liyan Warushavithana.

The Magistrate ordered the suspect to be released on two sureties of Rs. 1 million each and also imposed a travel ban on him.

Karunanayake was arrested when he appeared before CIABOC to provide a statement in connection with the investigation.

CIABOC told court that the case concerned three employees recruited on contract during Karunanayake’s tenure as Finance Minister from 12 January 2015 to 22 May 2017.

Investigators alleged that Karunanayake, together with then NLB Chairman Shyamala Perera, recruited two Coordinating Officers and a Management Assistant using NLB funds, purportedly for a special project of the Finance Ministry.

CIABOC alleged that the three employees performed no services for the NLB but were paid salaries and allowances by the institution, resulting in a financial loss. It alleged that they had instead been deployed for Karunanayake’s political activities.

The Commission sought his remand, alleging that he had acted together with the first suspect to influence witnesses.

CIABOC also told court that Karunanayake had been directed on four occasions to appear before the Commission but had failed to do so. Officers subsequently visited his residence on 29 August to conduct an inquiry.

According to CIABOC, officers were informed that Karunanayake had travelled to Nuwara Eliya for his daughter’s wedding, but subsequent investigations indicated that he was in Hambantota.

Charges have been filed against Karunanayake for the alleged offence of corruption under Section 70 of the Bribery Act, as amended by Act No. 20 of 1994.

Appearing for Karunanayake, Senior Counsel Asoka Weerasooriya sought bail on medical grounds and told court that his client had five stents and could require three more, citing medical reports from an examination in Singapore on 26 August. He also cited sleep apnoea, cellulitis and diabetes.

Counsel also submitted that the first suspect had already been granted bail and that there was no reason for Karunanayake to evade court proceedings.

After considering the submissions, the Additional Magistrate ordered Karunanayake’s release on bail.

title: A Negombo homestay’s sign-language tourism model goes international | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 1 September 2026 03:50
-     - 20

Nine years ago, a small guesthouse in Negombo began hosting guests the way almost no Sri Lankan property had before: entirely in sign language. That guesthouse, Lilly Palace Villa, has since welcomed more than 1,000 travellers from over 15 countries and holds a 4.8-star rating, and it is now the foundation of what its founders hope will become one of the island’s newer tourism export categories.

Ceylon Deaf Adventures (CDA), the Negombo-based inclusive travel enterprise that grew out of that homestay, has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with DeafVentures of Germany. Announced on August 20, the agreement is understood to be the first cross-border Deaf tourism partnership formalised by a Sri Lankan operator, and it converts an already-working relationship into a structured, ongoing one.

The two companies had already run a joint inbound tour before the MOU was signed , a fully accessible itinerary for confirmed German Deaf travellers, guided in sign language from the moment they landed to the moment they left. The agreement now gives that collaboration a framework to continue: CDA and DeafVentures will jointly develop, market and operate Deaf tourism packages connecting the two countries.

Deaf and hard-of-hearing travellers make up a sizeable, and largely unaddressed, segment of global tourism demand. The gap has rarely been about attitude, it is infrastructure: few destinations have guides, operators or accommodation providers who work natively in sign language rather than treating accessibility as an afterthought. By CDA’s own reading of the global Deaf travel landscape, no other dedicated inbound Deaf tourism operator exists anywhere in South Asia, leaving the field largely open.

That matters commercially because Sri Lankan tourism competes on relatively thin margins against every other sun-and-culture destination. A niche with almost no direct regional competition, unusually high traveller loyalty, and a tightly networked international community , the kind that produces referrals rather than one-off bookings, is a different kind of proposition. Germany already anchors CDA’s inbound numbers, and DeafVentures supplies the source-market credibility and distribution needed to turn that into a recurring, packaged pipeline rather than occasional group visits.

Behind the partnership is a personal story. Founder and CEO Praveen Waas is a CODA - a Child of Deaf Adults raised moving between the Deaf and hearing worlds, and fluent in Sinhala, Tamil, English and sign language. Lilly Palace Villa, run by his family since 2017, was Sri Lanka’s first Deaf-friendly homestay; CDA, formally launched in November 2025, was built to carry that same model  sign-language guiding paired with accessible logistics and Deaf-owned hospitality , beyond a single guesthouse. It has since hosted several Deaf tourist groups, and the DeafVentures MOU marks the first time that model has been extended into a formal international partnership.

It is precisely this combination  a commercially defensible niche, a first-mover position, and a measurable inclusion outcome  that tends to catch the attention of development partners, impact investors and SDG-aligned funders.

“This MOU is bigger than two companies. It’s the first bridge between Sri Lanka and the global Deaf community, built in our own language. We’re proving that accessibility isn’t a cost  it’s a market, and it’s one Sri Lanka can lead,” said Praveen Waas.

title: Electric shuttle service proposed to protect Horton Plains environment | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 1 September 2026 03:48
-     - 14

Authorities have proposed introducing an Electric Vehicle (EV) shuttle service within Horton Plains National Park to reduce vehicle emissions, carbon footprints and noise pollution.

The proposal was made during a special field observation tour and progress review discussion held at Horton Plains on 29 August, chaired by Environment Deputy Minister Anton Jayakody.

Under the proposed system, dedicated parking facilities would be established near the park’s entrance gates, with visitors transported into the park using electric shuttle vehicles.

The initiative is aimed at minimising the environmental impact and wildlife disturbance caused by conventional vehicles, while providing visitors with a quieter and more environmentally friendly experience.

Authorities expect the proposed system to contribute to the protection of the park’s sensitive ecosystem while supporting sustainable tourism.

Horton Plains, a UNESCO World Heritage site, is home to a unique and fragile ecosystem that is particularly vulnerable to human activity and environmental disturbances.

The proposal forms part of a broader program to modernise infrastructure and establish a sustainable eco-tourism model at the national park.

title: Horton Plains to introduce daily visitor limits and online booking | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 1 September 2026 03:47
-     - 17

Authorities are planning to introduce daily visitor limits and an online advance booking system at Horton Plains National Park as part of measures to reduce environmental pressure on the sensitive ecosystem.

The proposal was discussed during a special joint field observation tour and progress review meeting held on 29 August at Horton Plains, chaired by Environment Deputy Minister Anton Jayakody.

Officials said an online time-slot booking system would allow authorities to regulate the number of visitors entering the park at any given time and improve visitor management.

An adjusted pricing strategy is also being considered to reduce excessive visitor pressure while encouraging high-value, environmentally responsible tourism.

Horton Plains is a UNESCO World Heritage site known for its unique biodiversity and highly sensitive ecosystem.

The measures are part of a broader program aimed at developing a sustainable eco-tourism model while ensuring the long-term conservation of the national park.

The meeting was attended by Environment Ministry Secretary K.R. Uduwawala, senior officials from the Department of Wildlife Conservation and Department of Forest Conservation, and field officers including the Horton Plains Park Warden.

title: Cabinet clears Rs.1.24 b six travel counter contracts at BIA lobby | Daily FT
summary:
Tuesday, 1 September 2026 03:46
-     - 12

The Cabinet of Ministers has approved the awarding of contracts worth over Rs. 1.24 billion for the operation of six tourist service counters at the arrival lobby of Bandaranaike International Airport (BIA) in Katunayake, for three years.

Speaking at the post-Cabinet meeting media briefing last week, Cabinet Spokesman and Minister Dr. Nalinda Jayatissa said the move follows a National Competitive Bidding Procedure initiated by Airport and Aviation Services (Sri Lanka) Ltd.

The selected companies include: Casons Travels Ltd., (Rs. 251.03 million), Ayubowan Tours and Travels Ltd., (Rs. 171.53 million), Avawia Tours Ltd., (Rs. 189.66 million), JNW Lanka Tours (Rs. 209.67 million), Ceylon Arrivals Ltd., (Rs. 183.60 million) and 

Explore Vacations and Travels Ltd., (Rs. 234.73 million).

“A total of 19 bids were received in response to the call for tenders to operate the service counters located in the vacant lobby area in front of the arrivals terminal of BIA. After a thorough evaluation, six bidders who submitted the most responsive proposals were selected for the utilisation of the respective areas for a period of three years,” he added.

Dr. Jayatissa said the new tourist service counters are expected to offer a range of services to incoming travellers, contributing to an improved visitor experience and boosting tourism industry and economy.

The proposal to this effect was submitted by Ports, Shipping and Aviation Minister Anura Karunathilake.
